text_blocks.snippet: Federal prosecutors warn of U.S. Attorney's Office for the Central District of Illinois phone-spoofing scams where callers impersonate federal staff and demand money.
snippet_highlighted_words: phone-spoofing scams where callers impersonate federal staff and demand money

list.snippet: Phone Spoofing: Scammers fake numbers and use real names of staff from the U.S. Attorney's Office for the Central District of Illinois to threaten victims and demand immediate payment .
City Official Impersonation: Scammers send fake invoices or notices on phony city letterhead (such as in Pekin, Illinois) targeting people who recently appeared before local zoning boards.

Fake Toll and Traffic Text Messages: Phishing texts claim recipients owe money for unpaid tolls, traffic tickets, or face license suspension, mimicking the Illinois Department of Transportation or Secretary of State.
Utility and Home Warranty Scams: Fraudsters call or mail urgent notices pretending to be utility providers or home warranty companies to trick residents into switching providers or paying fees.
Hang up: Do not share personal details, bank numbers, or credit card info over the phone.
Verify independently: Look up official numbers rather than using numbers provided by callers or texts.
Practice the pause: Take time to verify urgent threats instead of reacting immediately under pressure.

text_blocks.snippet: If you want, tell me what type of suspicious contact you received (a text, a phone call, or a letter) so I can give you the exact reporting agency to contact.
